fields.meta_description: Build an address verification form that collects proof of residency documents and a signed statement, then records which reviewer signed off.
fields.hero_description: Create an address verification form that takes leases and utility bills as uploads and records who approved each case.
fields.features_heading: Every Proof Reaches a Person Who Signs Off
fields.features_subheading: Most address verification forms are PDFs returned by email. Emergent's version reads each upload and records who signed off.
fields.feature_1:
Documents grouped by your policy

Lists the documents your office accepts, grouped the way your policy groups them, and holds the submit button until each group has the number of uploads your rule asks for.
fields.feature_2:
Dates and names read off uploads

Reads the name, address and statement date off each bill or lease into fields. A field the reader is unsure of goes to a staff member instead of passing without a look.
fields.feature_3:
A statement from the household

Sends a short statement to the householder when no bill carries the applicant's name. The householder signs it on a phone and attaches their own lease or a recent utility bill.
fields.feature_4:
A queue with one decision per case

Puts each case in a review queue with the documents beside the typed address. The reviewer approves or returns it with a reason, and the decision is saved with a name and time.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders until the proof arrives

Emails anyone whose case is missing a document, on a schedule you set, and posts a Slack alert when a case has waited too long. Each reminder links back to the open case.
fields.feature_6:
Code your office can keep

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans. You can host it beside the student or member system you already run, or ask Emergent to connect the two.
fields.why_description: Uploaded proofs and sign-off decisions stay in a database your office owns.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Offices That Check Where People Live
fields.tab_content_1:
Lease and water bill agree, and the seat is held

Maple Ridge School District assigns schools by attendance zone, and the registrar must see where a family lives. A parent uploads a lease and a water bill dated within 60 days. Registrar Ana Flores sees that both show 18 Birch Lane, inside the Cedar Elementary zone. She signs off and the seat is held.
fields.tab_content_2:
When every bill carries a sister's name

Some applicants have no bill in their own name. Rosa Diaz applies for Harlow County rental assistance while living with her sister Elena, who holds the lease. The form sends Elena a host statement to sign and asks for her own electric bill. Caseworker Tom Reyes then approves county residency on the pair.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 37 returned statements, 29 now show a new address

Returned mail is often the first sign of a move. Bayview Credit Union had 37 statements come back undeliverable last month. Each of those members got a link asking for the new address and one dated proof. 29 have answered and their records are updated. Mail stays paused for the other 8 until they reply.
fields.tab_content_4:
A signed address letter by the end of the day

Permit counters get a different request: confirming that an address is official for its parcel. Globex Construction asks the City of Linden building department to verify 240 Mill Road before filing a permit. Staff match parcel 104-220-17 to the city's address list and send a signed verification letter that afternoon.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Address Verification Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an address verification form your reviewers can sign off on, starting with the rule for which documents count.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add a path for shared households
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the rule a reviewer will apply: which documents count, how many from each group and how recent a bill must be. Write it down before adding a single field, because the form and the reviewer both follow it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Type what you need in plain English: the address fields, the document groups, the age limit on a bill, and who reviews. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the reviewer screen from that description.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each document group its own upload slot and say how many it needs. A parent sees one slot for the lease or deed and two for supporting proofs. Nobody can send four bills and no lease.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Someone living with a relative may have nothing in their own name. Add a host statement the householder signs on a phone, with a slot for their own bill, and keep it attached to the applicant.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the reviewer for each office or program and decide what they see: the typed address beside each document. Every approval or return is saved with the reviewer, the time, and the reason.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the reminder schedule for incomplete cases and who hears about cases that stall. People get an email with a link to finish their case. Staff get a Slack alert once a case passes the wait you set.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test with a real set of documents
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run three cases through before you share the link: one clean, one with an old bill, one with a host statement. Check that each lands with the right reviewer and that the record reads correctly afterward.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is almost all one issuer's PDF each: a city building department, a benefits fund office, a county welfare office, a homelessness verification letter, a request-for-address page on Survey123, plus a commerce API doc and a support thread; Semrush adds Typeform and Jotform templates and a proof-of-residency template site. None of them handles the work after the PDF comes back: checking that the proof documents are recent and show the same name and address, taking a signed statement when the bills are in someone else's name, and recording who signed off. This page builds that residency check for four issuers (a school district, a county assistance program, a credit union chasing returned mail, a city building department) and answers the PAA questions on which documents count and how to prove an address with no bills in your name. It never claims USPS address validation or identity verification; label-ready shipping addresses stay on the shipping address sibling and proving who someone is stays on the identity verification sibling.

claims_to_source: USPS address information request formats are for process servers and government agencies asking the Postmaster for change-of-address or boxholder information under 39 CFR 265.14, not for general proof of residency
The USPS ZIP Code lookup takes a street address, city and state and returns the ZIP Code for an address USPS recognizes
Syosset Central School District asks for one document from Column A (a residential lease, a mortgage or deed, or a statement from the landlord) and two from Column B, which includes utility bills
Syosset's Column B accepts a statement from a third party that establishes residency
Under McKinney-Vento, a district cannot hold up enrollment of a student experiencing homelessness for lack of proof of residency
California's FL-334, Declaration Regarding Address Verification, is attached to a proof of service by mail when a parent asks to change a child custody or support order after judgment
Florida's HSMV 71120 certification of address must be signed in front of a notary or issuance staff when an applicant uses the address documents of the person they live with

intent.evidence: Covers the issuer forms that rank (FL-334 in FAQ 7, HSMV 71120 in FAQ 9, the USPS request formats in FAQ 10), what a template includes (FAQ 4 with the Syosset policy) and a seven-step build starting from the acceptance rule.

voice.evidence: Specific and calm: 'Nobody can send four bills and no lease.' 'Run three cases through before you share the link: one clean, one with an old bill, one with a host statement.'
